title: The costs of Massa's strategy to contain free dollars and "make it" to December
text:
The blue dollar is sold this Tuesday without changes at $486 in the caves of the microcenter of Buenos Aires. In the last few weeks, the Government managed to achieve an exchange rate stability that surprised the Buenos Aires city without drawing up a new soybean dollar 4 program, by means of a tightening of the exchange rate, intervention in the dollar futures market and betting heavily on foreign financing.

In this way, the national government is playing an "all or nothing" game to try to avoid new scenarios of exchange rate stress that could have a full impact on an already accelerated inflation, putting one foot (or both) in a hyperinflationary terrain.

To this end, Massa drew up a plan with his team to, at least, reach the next Simultaneous and Mandatory Open Primary Elections (PASO) with the official dollar "accompanying" inflation and the free dollars strongly intervened.

"The only money the government really has today to intervene the CCL and the MEP is the swap it got from China. From the IMF disbursement, it will be necessary to see how the negotiations turn out to determine whether or not Argentina could use part of those funds to intervene in the exchange market", expressed the economic analyst, Sergio Rodriguez. The clamp for provinces and industries

The worrying exchange rate situation led to a new restriction by the Central Bank and this time the provinces were the ones affected. As it was already applied to the private sector in 2021, now the provinces will only be able to access the MULC to face debt maturities for 40% of the capital amortizations.

Although there are 14 provinces that issued debt in hard currency, only seven of them have to pay principal maturities in 2023 for a total of u$s462 million, so the savings of the measure is less than 280 million dollars, affecting mainly Córdoba, which will have to face its maturities of a little more than u$s70 million with its own resources.

Furthermore, the new restrictions of the Central Bank to access the MULC not only affect the forms of financing, but also directly compromise the industry, since the Central Bank's Foreign Exchange Market Evolution Report shows the evolution of the debt forced to importers.

In this context, since February 2022 a difference can be seen between imports accrued and those effectively paid. This represents a forced debt accumulated by the private sector because they are not granted access to foreign currency in the MULC. Thus, the importers' commercial debt increased by u$s370 million, accumulating u$s2,700 million so far in 2023 and u$s10,600 million since February 2022. Costs of the measure

Analysts of the Buenos Aires city warned that the successive regulations on foreign trade force the readjustment of the market, but "it manages to rearm itself and, logically, it presses again to obtain dollars at half the price".

If access to the official dollar is perceived as inaccessible, importers will use financial dollars as a reference to fix the replacement cost and this will have an impact on inflation. Thus, a supine victory in the foreign exchange market may have its correlate in inflationary acceleration.

For Rodriguez, the macroeconomic fundamentals are increasingly complicated: the nominal rate is accelerating, net reserves are not increasing in real terms at the pace needed, affected by the terrible drought that promises that this year's harvest will be considerably lower than last year's, leading our country to enter a recessionary terrain in economic activity due to the strong restrictions imposed on imports.

"In this context, it is not surprising the greater restrictions to the provinces and imports in order to manage the meager stock of reserves, which we estimate at -US$1,600 million", warned the economic consultant. Intervention in the Rofex

Futures contracts continue to fall and in the last 30 days they plummeted 34% on average. The drop was seen almost exclusively in the longest contracts, while the June and July contracts maintain a high implicit devaluation rate of 10% and 12%, respectively.

"Short contracts continue to 'price' such high devaluations, that the fall is due to the BCRA intervention and that exchange rate tensions are still in force", explained a recognized Alyc.

The broker pointed out that the average implicit devaluation rate for the next 12 months plummeted to 9.1% monthly and 185% annualized, while "a week ago it was 10.0% monthly and 214% annualized.

"Thus, the implied rate curve compressed by another 453 basis points and looks flatter than ever with the BCRA intervening on the long side. Contracts yield 121% and 138% between June and July, 150% and 152% between August and November, 165% and 175% from December onwards", said Alyc. How much is the blue dollar quoted today

The blue dollar is at $486 for sale and $482 for purchase. How financial dollars trade

In the stock market, the cash settled dollar (CCL) is traded at $495.84; while the MEP is offered at $472.29. What is the price of the official dollar?

The retail dollar trades at $253.83 average.

In the wholesale market, the U.S. currency is around $242.50.

Thus, the dollar with the 30% surcharge -included in the PAÍS tax-, averages $329.98 per unit, and with the 35% advance payment on account of Income Tax on the purchase of foreign currency, at $418.82.

Meanwhile, the dollar for tourism abroad -which has a 45% tax rate- is at $444.20, while for purchases over 300 dollars -which has an additional tax of 25%- it is at $507.66. The exchange rate gap

Finally, the exchange rate gap between the average retail dollar published by the BCRA and the different exchange rates is as follows: Blue: 91%. CCL: 95%. MEP: 89%.

title: Massa ratified that the swap is to consolidate the yuan "as an investment instrument".
text:
The Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa, assured before the 40 largest companies in China that the hydrocarbons sector "is experiencing an explosion" with Vaca Muerta, said that in three years the country's economic matrix will have "a turnaround" due to lithium exports, and said that the recent currency swap extended and renewed with Beijing "is key" because it consolidates "the yuan as an investment instrument".During a forum organized by the embassy in Beijing, Massa stated that Argentina is going through a process of transformation of its economic matrix, which until now only had the agro-industrial complex as the main export pole.

He also highlighted the importance of having renewed the swap between the BCRA and the People's Bank of China, a measure that strengthens the reserves.

In a 27-minute speech before construction, telecommunications and mining giants such as Huawei, PowerChina, Gezhouba and Tibet Summit Resources, the Minister pointed out that the extension of the BCRA agreement with the Chinese counterpart entity is "key" for investments from that country and, at the same time, "enables Argentina" to "use mechanisms for all kinds of interventions".

On that point, he said that the three-year extension of the currency agreement "allows companies from the People's Republic of China the opportunity to develop a flow of investments (to Argentina) on the basis of the mobilization of the yuan", and at the same time "enables Argentina, not only to use it for commercial and foreign exchange investment flows, but also to use mechanisms of our Central Bank for all kinds of investments".

The agreement with the Popular Bank of China (PBoC) signed yesterday implied the renewal for three years of the swap for a total amount of 130 billion yuan (equivalent to US$ 19 billion) and with a free availability percentage of US$ 10 billion, with US$ 5 billion deposited in the BCRA and a second tranche of US$ 5 billion already approved for all uses.

During his presentation, Massa also referred to the prospects that are opening up for Argentina going from being "an energy importer to a net energy exporter", with an export potential of US$ 20 billion for the next three years.

The head of the Treasury Palace also mentioned "the critical processes" that the country is cyclically going through in economic matters: he attributed them to the trade deficit and indebtedness, but also indicated that the process of asset formation abroad (capital flight) is a consequence of the lack of credibility in the peso.

Referring to Argentina and "the recurrent changes in debt programs", Massa affirmed that the trigger for the country to take on debt is the impossibility of "financing public expenditure".

For this reason, he considered it necessary that "the State invests well, with balance and responsibility".

Regarding foreign trade, and with dozens of representatives of Chinese companies present in the auditorium of the Seasons Hotel, Massa proposed that the commercial relationship between Buenos Aires and Beijing progressively advance towards "a balanced trade balance".

This, he said, will allow Argentina to "project a trade surplus so as not to experience situations of (financial) stress".

Massa was accompanied by the Argentine ambassador in Beijing, Sabino Vaca Narvaja; the head of YPF, Pablo González; the Minister of Transportation, Diego Giuliano; the Secretary of Energy, Flavia Royon; the Secretary of International Financial Relations and head of Indec, Marco Lavagna, and the Secretary of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries, Juan José Bahillo.

The event was attended by the innovation giant Huawei, as well as the construction companies Gezhouba, China Energy Engineering Corporation, China Machinery Engineering and PowerChina, all four in the engineering sector.

Other companies present were China Railway Construction (railways), China Electric Power Equipment and Technology (electricity), ZTE (telecommunications), DiDi (digital mobility application) and Xiaomi (cell phones).

Also in attendance were Tibet Summit Resources (the world's largest nickel and stainless steel miner), CNNC China Zhongyuan Engineering (nuclear power), Chery (automotive), Shandong Gold Group (gold mining) and Norinco (defense technology).

Other companies represented at the forum were China National Machinery Import and Export (infrastructure), Citic Construction (construction), CRRC Sifang (railway equipment), Great Wall (automotive), CETC (telecommunications) and Tsingshan (mining).

The list was completed with Oppo electronics, Goldwing (wind energy) and Ganfeng (mining company specialized in lithium), as part of a list of more than forty private and public companies, which also included Argentine wineries with presence in the Chinese market, such as Colomé and Catena Zapata.

In the final part of his speech, Massa valued the fact that more and more tourists from China are visiting Argentina, and said that the Government is working together with Aerolíneas Argentinas so that the company can make the first direct flight to Beijing with a stopover in Auckland, which will reduce the flight time by ten hours (to travel between Buenos Aires and the Chinese capital today it is essential to make a stopover).

Finally, the Minister of Economy acknowledged as a problem that the entry of Chinese citizens into the country requires a visa application process that can take up to 90 days.

On this point, he promised that Argentina will make an effort to reduce the processing time to 15 days.

The entry Massa ratified that the swap is to consolidate the yuan "as an investment instrument" was posted first on Diario San Rafael.

title: Massa stated that the swap with China is to strengthen the yuan "as an investment instrument".
text:
Sergio Massa, stated this Saturday before the 40 largest hydrocarbon companies in China that the sector "is experiencing an explosion" with Vaca Muerta. The Minister of Economy estimated that in three years the Argentine economic matrix will have "a turnaround" due to lithium exports, and said that the recent extended and renewed currency swap with Beijing "is key" because it consolidates "the yuan as an investment instrument".

During a forum organized by the embassy in Beijing, the minister stated that Argentina is going through a process of transformation of its economic matrix, which until now only had the agro-industrial complex as the main export pole. And he highlighted the importance of having renewed the swap between the BCRA and the People's Bank of China, a measure that strengthens the reserves.According to a Télam article signed by Martín Piqué, Massa spoke for 27 minutes before representatives of companies such as Huawei, PowerChina, Gezhouba and Tibet Summit Resources. He pointed out that the extension of the Central Bank's agreement with its Chinese counterpart is "key" for the Asian giant's investments and "enables Argentina" to "use mechanisms for all kinds of interventions".On that point, he said that the three-year extension of the currency agreement "allows companies from the People's Republic of China the opportunity to develop an investment flow (to Argentina) on the basis of the mobilization of the yuan", and in parallel "enables Argentina, not only to the use for commercial and foreign exchange flows of investments, but also to mechanisms of use of our Central Bank for all kinds of investments".Regarding foreign trade, and with dozens of representatives of Chinese companies present in the auditorium of the Seasons Hotel, Massa proposed that the commercial relationship between Buenos Aires and Beijing progressively advance towards "a balanced trade balance". This, he said, will allow Argentina to "project a trade surplus so as not to experience situations of (financial) stress".

With the tourism sectorLater, Massa closed his tour by participating in the Investment and Tourism Business Forum, where he presented the opportunities offered by Argentina.

On his last day of activities in the city of Beijing, the national official was present at the meeting that gathered the main tourism agencies of the Asian giant. In this framework, the head of the Treasury Palace emphasized that more and more Chinese tourists choose Argentina because of its natural destinations and the possibility of making payments in their local currency thanks to the promotion of direct exchange of yuan.

"This phenomenon leads to a positive impact on the country's foreign currency income, since today China is one of the world's main tourist issuers and one of the biggest spenders," the Ministry of Economy remarked in a statement.

During his presentation, Massa anticipated that the first direct flight to China will be launched this year, in principle with code-sharing, which will reduce the flight time by 10 hours and will improve connectivity between both countries.

He also commented that the aim is to facilitate the granting of visas, seeking to reduce the process to one week. In addition, the most popular electronic payment methods in China will be allowed to be used in Argentina.

He also remarked that Argentina is the first South American country authorized by China to receive its tourists within the framework of a pilot program presented to relaunch global tourism.

According to data from Argentina's Tourism Information System, 7.4 million foreign tourists will enter Argentina during 2022. Meanwhile, China ranks 16th in the ranking of inbound tourism in Argentina (same position as 2018) with a total of almost 76 thousand arrivals in 2019, with an average spending per stay per person of US$ 1,860 and an average daily expenditure of US$ 122.

The development of Chinese tourism in Argentina is one of the strategic vectors to solve the income of foreign currency, and through these incentives the country could go from receiving an average of 70 thousand tourists per year to almost 500 thousand, which would imply a strong income of foreign currency due to the spending made on average by visitors coming from the Asian country: only in the weekend of May 1, about 274 million people made tourism trips in China.

title: Massa ratified that part of the swap with China is "freely available".
text:
The Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa, closed his tour in China with a balance of the work agenda he developed during five days in Shanghai and Beijing. There he referred to the swap and ratified that the increase of 5,000 million dollars are freely available and can be used to intervene in the price of the dollar. This is in response to the criticism of the opposition and the request of Juntos por el Cambio to go to Congress to report on the agreement.

Before 40 businessmen who attended the Investment and Tourism Business Forum held at the Four Seasons Hotel in the Chinese capital, the same hotel where the Argentine National Team will stay on June 15, he assured that both the current 5,000 million and the new 5,000 billion can be used "for all kinds of financial operations". In other parts of his speech, he highlighted the complementarity and opportunities for both economies and announced that in order to promote tourism they are working on a direct flight from the Asian country to Argentina and on reducing the visa time from 90 to 15 days.

Regarding the new agreement for the currency swap, he said: "It enables the Argentine Republic not only to use it for trade flows but also to use the instrument as an instrument for the flow of foreign currency for investments and also for mechanisms to use our Central Bank for all kinds of interventions". Later on, he added: "Argentina has two great challenges to overcome, and undoubtedly, the appearance of investment flows, currency swaps, and above all, exports and imports, using the yuan, allows us to break the idea that the cycles of difficulty are tied to two issues: to the formation of foreign assets, due to lack of confidence in our currency, and there the swap and the use of the yuan as an instrument or mechanism for investments and, on the other hand, in the formation of domestic assets, the recurring mechanisms or changes in debt programs based on the financing of public spending.

After the announcement made by Massa yesterday with the President of the Central Bank, Miguel Pesce, the opposition asked for answers on the details of the new swap that will have a three-year term for 19 billion dollars. Congressman Martin Tetaz requested to summon both officials to confirm not only the renewal of the loan with the People's Bank of China but also the term, the interest rate and the new conditions.

Flights to ChinaDuring his presentation, Massa anticipated that Aerolíneas Argentinas is working for the first direct flight to China this year, in principle with code-sharing, with a stopover in Auckland (New Zealand), which will reduce the flight time by 10 hours. The flights, which cost around one million dollars according to the estimates of the delegation, will take place every 15 days.

In line with this timeframe, the granting of visas will be reduced from 90 to 15 days. This is subject to a resolution of the Foreign Ministry, which has already been requested by the embassy and which Massa will try to speed up in the next few days. In addition, the most popular electronic means of payment in China will be allowed to be used in Argentina. "That this back and forth that we feel far away because of the distance that separates us is reduced by the political decision, by the investment, but above all by the intelligence to connect us", said Massa.

Among the companies that listened to the Minister, from the Chinese tourism sector, Ctrip, UTour and Qunar participated. Also present were the energy companies China Energy and Powerchina, the engineering and construction company China Gezhouba Group, the construction company China Machinery Enginecring Corporation (CMEC), the transport company DIDI, the electronics manufacturer Xiaomi and the cell phone company Huawei, among others. The Minister of Economy was accompanied by the Argentine Ambassador to China, Sabino Vaca Narvaja; the Minister of Transportation, Diego Giuliano; the Secretary of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries, Juan José Bahillo; and the President of YPF, Pablo González.

The head of the Palace of Finance emphasized that more and more Chinese tourists are choosing Argentina because of its natural destinations and the possibility of making payments in their local currency thanks to the promotion of direct exchange of yuans. According to data from the Argentine Tourism Information System, 7.4 million foreign tourists entered Argentina in 2022. China ranks 16th in the ranking of inbound tourism in the country with a total of almost 76 thousand arrivals, with an average spending per stay per person of 1,860 dollars.

InvestmentsIn his speech, Massa highlighted the investments made during these days. Regarding mining, he explained that he expects the development of the sector to allow a change in the energy matrix and to be a pillar in the country's economy. "We aspire to have exports for 20 billion dollars in 2026 and that from 203 they will have added value for another 20 billion", specified the minister.

Then, he affirmed that "gas is going to be the transition energy in the coming years" towards renewable energies. He reminded that Argentina has the second shale gas field and the fourth shale oil field. Energy was one of the main topics of the official's tour. "In terms of investments, investment in the sector grew 42% and it is one of the great tractors that compensates one of the worst situations that Argentina is going through due to the drought", he mentioned.

Massa pointed out that in the next three years the country will achieve "a turnaround" in terms of energy balance. "We are going to go from being energy importers for almost 20 billion dollars to being exporters for more than 20 billion dollars", he assured. And he highlighted the developments of the Néstor Kirchner gas pipeline and the northern reversal.

Finally, he sent a message to businessmen inviting them to look at the long term: "The Chinese culture, its government and reform project looks at development thought and planned for generations. Development is built thinking in the long term, added value is built thinking intergenerationally. Cooperation and brotherhood between countries is built on the basis of the strength of a bond on several fronts as we have to face it".

title: Alberto Fernandez met with Lula and reached agreement for Brazil to finance imports
text:
President Alberto Fernández and the Brazilian President, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, held a bilateral meeting on Tuesday, during which the leader of the Petista party confirmed that the National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES) will finance the imports of pipes and steel sheets manufactured by Brazilian companies to be used in the Néstor Kirchner Gas Pipeline.

The meeting took place at the end of the summit of South American presidents held in Brasilia, where the Brazilian head of state told his Argentine counterpart that there are no longer any obstacles for the BNDES to intervene in foreign trade transactions with Argentina and that progress will be made with the financing to allow the importation of Brazilian products.

According to the Brazilian Foreign Ministry, financing will be provided for the export of pipes and steel plates produced in Brazil to be used in the second phase of the President Néstor Kirchner gas pipeline (Saliqueló - San Jeronimo section), and other parts of the northern gas pipeline, Salta - GNEA, Aldea Brasileira - Uruguaiana and San Jeronimo - Santa Fe.

In this way, the financing could reach an amount of up to u$s600 million and would allow Argentina to avoid the use of Central Bank reserves in times of foreign currency shortage.

Credit from the BRICS bank Regarding the possibility that the BRICS Bank led by Dilma Rouseff may facilitate financing to Argentina, Lula revealed that there are difficulties for the entity to change its regulations to proceed with the granting of a credit to the Argentine government, one of the items on the agenda of the Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa, during his visit to China .

The president recalled that at the G7 meeting in Japan he spoke "with many presidents" to intercede with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to help Argentina "not to have a knife in its neck".

In this sense, he added that the same request and the argument to renegotiate new conditions after the drought was made to the head of the IMF, Kristalina Georgieva.

Lula assured, in this sense, that the expectations that the New Development Bank (NDB), the Bank of the Brics (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) could act as a guarantor for the exports of Brazilian companies to Argentina in view of the problems in collecting payment due to the restrictions of dollars were reduced.

"We agreed with the president of China, Xi Jinping, to talk to the Brics Bank to change an article (number 7) that prohibits financing to countries not affiliated to the bank. That meeting of the bank took place and there seems to be difficulty in doing so," Lula said.

Energy integration In addition, the presidents also discussed different mechanisms to deepen energy integration between the two countries, so that Argentina can improve the terms of payment for thermal energy imports.

President Lula celebrated that, thanks to the availability of Brazilian generators, Brazil will be able to guarantee the supply of electricity from thermal sources to Argentina in the coming months and expressed the expectation that the Argentine government will find prices and conditions with Brazilian suppliers that imply the least impact on Argentine foreign currency.

On the other hand, they discussed the progress of the bilateral talks on the future management model of the São Borja-Santo Tomé Bridge, whose current concession expires in August. There is agreement between the two presidents that the bridge is strategic for bilateral trade.

title: The Government decided to cut "the financial dollar "loop" and another fight broke out between Massa and Pesce.
text:
This Thursday, the Government gave the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA) the order not to intervene in bond trading and allowed the MEP and cash with settlement dollar prices to rise. Financial dollars jumped 6.6% and 2.5% respectively and set a record closing price. The case generated a new fight between the Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa, and the head of the Central Bank, Miguel Pesce.

According to TN, the decision to let prices move without the Central Bank's intervention responded to the Government's intention to make its actions in the market less predictable in order to cut some speculative maneuvers that began to take place and also to take maximum care of the dollars, when the net reserves were negative.

The Economy detected that there were operations that took advantage of the Government's intervention to make a money difference. In stock market jargon, these transactions are known as "rulo".

One of these strategies was to buy Mep dollars with the AL30 bond, in which the Government intervenes and therefore has a cheaper exchange rate. After the 24-hour parking, those dollars were used to buy a bill in foreign currency, which was then sold in pesos at a higher exchange rate. Thus, the investor took the difference.

The one who gave the order was Massa, who called directly to the vice-president of the BCRA, Lisandro Cleri, early in the morning. Before the opening of the markets, Cleri checked again with Massa. The answer was blunt: "Get out of the market".

The measure provoked the anger of the stockbrokers and the cueveros, who had losses for about U$S 45 million and went to complain to the head of the Central Bank. Pesce sent a message to Massa and then tried to call him on his cell phone. But Massa gave him a ticking off.

Hours later, Massa finally answered the phone. There were cross reproaches and Massa told Pesce "You can't handle a single one" and justified himself: "the stockbrokers had taken our time".

Back in April, Massa and Pesce had already had a hard confrontation between them due to the delays of the BCRA in the instrumentalization of the agricultural dollar. And another one on Saturday, when the whole economic team met after the INDEC announced the record inflation of 8.4% in April, the highest level since April 2002. Massa then blamed him for the BCRA's lack of reaction to the overheating of the dollar and prices in April.

title: Inflation: what is the diagnosis for Argentina of one of the world's leading investment banks?
text:
With each official inflation figure released by the Indec, market pessimism for the short term deepens and the diagnoses regarding the unavoidable need to apply a comprehensive stabilization plan are repeated.

Such analyses are circulating locally and also in the international arena, where Argentina is beginning to attract attention -although without arousing interest-, due to the imminent electoral process that will eventually determine the implementation of a new economic plan.

However, there is still a long way to go and warnings are coming from abroad. Once again, one of the main Wall Street banks, Goldman Sachs, prepared a note on the recent developments of the Argentine economy. The investment bank focused on the effect of the measures adopted by the economic team during the weekend, essentially the new interest rate hike, in addition to the intervention in the foreign exchange market to prevent the dollar's financial quotations from soaring. "It is difficult for transitory measures to help," he argued.

The report for Goldman Sachs clients written by economist Sergio Armella describes the critical outlook for the local economy. "The macroeconomic context in Argentina remains very complex. In our assessment, inflation is expected to remain in three digits, there are increasing levels of financial repression, and a significant slowdown in real activity is already being registered," said the analyst, who highlighted the Government's failure to meet the targets established in the agreement with the Monetary Fund. From that perspective, he highlighted that "policy credibility remains weak and the risk of an even more severe loss of monetary and price control is high".

The report thus refers to the failure to meet the fiscal and monetary targets of the program revised in March with the Fund. Paradoxically, the only goal achieved was the accumulation of reserves, after the requirement established last year was modified. This relaxation was agreed under the argument of the strong impact of the drought on the flow of foreign currency. However, the Fund still did not agree to modify the fiscal deficit target and, consequently, the monetary emission target. Both variables showed a significant deviation. The fiscal target, set at a deficit of $440 billion, was comfortably exceeded by an imbalance of $689 billion in the first three months of the year.

With respect to the Central Bank's financing of the Treasury, the target also became a dead letter: with the last drawing of temporary advances, the Central Bank issued $670 billion since March to finance the public accounts. This figure should be compared with an issuance ceiling set for the whole first half of the year by the IMF: $373 billion until the end of June.

That is what Goldman Sachs is referring to when it explains that "ultimately, the high inflation environment in Argentina reflects deep structural macroeconomic policy imbalances" and rules out that, with that approach, the latest measures adopted by Economía can have any degree of effectiveness. "Unless these imbalances are comprehensively addressed, it is difficult to expect that the policy of transitory measures will help to rebalance the economy in a meaningful and lasting way," said the bank's report.

The bank's diagnosis is related to the complaint expressed yesterday by the group that groups the creditors of the Argentine debt that entered the swap carried out by the former Minister of Economy, Martín Guzmán. "Argentina has zero credibility. There is no interest rate or intervention policy, price control or consumption stimulus that works under these circumstances. In fact, they make things worse. The solution is a stabilization plan: zero deficit, devaluation and free exchange rate" Argentina Exchange Bondholders argued in a post on Twitter.

title: How high will the dollar and inflation be at the end of the year, according to the report most consulted by the private sector?
text:
The projections of the regional consulting firm Latin Fcus assure that Argentina will have the worst performance in the region in 2023. According to this month's Latin Focus Consensus Forecast report, one of the most consulted and used by the private sector to make projections and measure what will happen with the variables of the Argentine economy -prepared on the forecasts of more than 50 economic consulting firms and local and foreign banks-, inflation will stand at 108.4% average by the end of the year and the official dollar will reach $391 in 2023 and $791 in 2024.

"After a deterioration in the economy driven by falling domestic demand in the fourth quarter of 2022, the economy likely remained stagnant in the first quarter. Inflation increased while the peso continued to depreciate markedly. In addition, consumer confidence remained deeply pessimistic," describes the report prepared by the consulting firm.

Inflation will average 108.4% by the end of the year and the official dollar will reach $391 in 2023 and $791 in 2024.

And then it lists a series of factors that further worsened the economic situation: "exports fell, interest rates soared and there was a severe drought. Moving to the second quarter, two additional rate hikes in April and still depressed consumer confidence, along with a declining peso, represent problems for activity."

They also noted that the country's reserves are at their lowest level in nearly seven years due to drought-stricken agricultural exports and foreign exchange interventions to support the peso.

"Argentina will have the worst performance in the region this year. GDP will fall amid galloping inflation, a free-falling peso, shrinking savings and sky-high interest rates. Global headwinds and drought will worsen the situation. Add to that the uncertainty in the run-up to the October general elections. Extremely high debt payment risks further cloud the outlook," the report warned.

Regarding the inflation rate, Latin Focus consultants highlighted that it is the highest since their records began. "Inflation rose to 108.8% in April, following 104.3% in March, which marked the highest inflation rate since our current records began. Average inflation is projected to be notably higher this year than in 2022 amid the depreciation of the peso and monetary financing of the fiscal deficit," they explained.

FocusEconomics panelists note two key risks: volatile energy prices and fiscal spending ahead of the October elections. As a result, they estimated that consumer prices will rise 108.4% on average in 2023, up 5.6 percentage points from the previous projection, published a month ago.

"After the strong upside surprise in April, we revised our central scenario for the future. We now assume monthly headline inflation of 8.1% per month on average through the end of the year. And we assume a correction in the official exchange rate by the end of 2023 when a new administration takes office in December," anticipated Lucila Barbeito and Diego Pereira, analysts at JPMorgan.

At the time of the report's closing, the Argentine peso was trading at $229 per dollar, a 6.7% monthly depreciation. "The Central Bank sticks to a managed floating exchange rate for the peso. Meanwhile, the parallel market dollar was quoted at $472 per USD. The peso should lose more ground amid prolonged monetary financing of the fiscal deficit," FocusEconomics panelists noted. All in all, they see the official dollar ending 2023 at $391 and by the end of 2024 it will reach 791 pesos.

Finally, the consultants anticipated that Argentina's GDP will contract by 2.4% during 2023, which represents a reduction of 0.5 percentage points compared to the previous month, and will expand by only 0.4% in 2024.

title: After rumors of new measures, the dollar closed higher
text:
The rumors that the Central Bank of Argentina (BCRA) will increase its intervention in the foreign exchange market and that it will manage the pace of the daily micro-devaluations of the peso generated doubts among economists, since the lack of official information led everyone to speculate on what could be the chosen path. For that reason, attention was focused yesterday on the behavior of the dollar in the different segments.

The free dollar gained nine pesos or 1.8% in its selling point, to $483 in the parallel market, its highest price since April 25. In the course of May, the blue dollar sustained an increase of 14 pesos or 3 percent.

With a wholesale dollar that rose 1.50 peso to $230.70, the exchange rate gap remained at 109.4 percent. In the last month, the rise of the official exchange rate reached 7.5%, while in the last year it accumulated an increase of 96.5%, in both cases, below the inflation rate.

"The gap between MEP and blue today is the main indicator of a massive dollarization of the black economy. The blue as a market must have tripled or quadrupled," said an experienced broker to the online newspaper Infobae.

Stock exchange dollars were also traded with a clear increase. Both the "contado con liquidación" and the MEP dollar gained close to four pesos, at $444.60 and $437.66, through the Global 2030 (GD30, species "C" and "D") in the PPT (Price-Time Priority) segment of ByMA (Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos), where the BCRA intervenes with the offer of its portfolio bonds.

Quotation and crawling peg

Opinions on the Central Bank's attitude towards the exchange rate are divided. On the one hand, some believe that if the pace of devaluation is not accelerated, the exchange rate backwardness puts pressure on the demand for dollars, so that the monthly variation should at least keep pace with inflation. On the other hand, there are those who believe that accelerating the devaluation to that pace (or increasing it in case the gap is to be narrowed) would boost inflation, since the US currency would stop working as an anchor for prices.

"April's inflation put a new dilemma to the exchange market. If the BCRA accelerates the devaluation, it will be adding fuel to the fire. If it delays the exchange rate to use it as an anchor, it will be selling cheaper and cheaper reserves, where the net reserves are already more than 1 billion dollars negative", considered Roberto Geretto, analyst at Fundcorp. "The situation is complex and the commandment 'thou shalt not devalue' has more and more costs, but devaluing without a plan may be a leap into the void. In this context, raising rates only serves to gain some time, at the cost of continuing to enlarge the Leliq ball," said the economist.

Economist Federico Glustein points out that, based on yesterday's quotation, the peso devaluated 0.57% in the whole weekend, a low level considering that, in the last 15 days, the variation of the official exchange rate is 3.5%, when the floor should be at least 8.5% monthly (in line with inflation).

The same is observed by Invecq's economist, Juan Pablo Albornoz, who points out that "looking at an average of the last 5 days, the Central Bank let the official dollar run at an annual effective rate (AER) of 99.8%, considering the compensation for the weekend, and, in the last 5 rounds, the crawling advanced to 101% per annum".

This is a level far behind the benchmark interest rates. Especially, taking into account that the new rate hike established that Leliqs will accrue an APR of 154.88% from now on. Thus, taking the month as a period of time, "the Central Bank is letting the official rate run at 5.9% effective monthly average in the last five days, far behind the rest of the prices of the economy", pointed out Albornoz.

The economist is of the opinion that, possibly, this deceleration that the BCRA is marking in the pace of devaluation of the peso price aims at cooling the inflationary inertia we are having, although he warns that "it is hardly sustainable if the real exchange rate level is to be maintained".

title: Rate hikes, exchange rate  intervention  and lower tariffs:  Argentina  tests strategies against inflation
text:
Argentina is no longer trying to lower inflation; it is at least trying to keep it from getting out of control. This Monday, the Government of Alberto Fernández will present a package of economic measures to defend the peso, discourage savings in dollars and add international reserves to the Central Bank. In five months there will be general elections and nobody expects a comprehensive stabilization plan or a change in expectations. It is a matter of reaching October with the ship afloat, while the responsibility for major surgery is transferred to the person who takes office on December 10. The polls take for granted that it will not be a Peronist. The Casa Rosada has tied its electoral future to a candidacy of the Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa. If Massa does not achieve economic results, he will hardly be a candidate.

April inflation reached 8.4% and raised the year-on-year inflation rate to 108.8%, the highest in 30 years. The CPI has not stopped rising for the last six months: 4.9% in November, 5.1% in December, 6.0% in January, 6.6% in February and 7.7% in March. April strengthened the rise and anticipated a May that will be dangerously close to double digits. There is no talk of hyperinflation yet, but the ghost of the great crisis of 1989 is there.

In March, the Central Bank raised the reference interest rate from 81% to 91%. This Monday a new increase came into effect, up to 97%. At the same time, the Ministry of Economy announced that it will "increase intervention in the foreign exchange market and will manage the pace of the crawling peg", that is, the policy of daily devaluation of the peso against the dollar in the official exchange rate, as required by the IMF. The issue is to convince Argentines to keep their savings in pesos: the Central Bank has its reserves close to zero and can no longer supply the foreign exchange market.

To the tourniquet on the outflow of dollars, the Government will add a new negotiation with the International Monetary Fund (it intends to advance 11,000 million dollars foreseen for the end of the year), increase the swap with China and the support of Brazil. The IMF has so far limited itself to welcome the "constructive" negotiations with Argentina. China has already agreed to pay imports in yuan for some US$ 5 billion; Minister Massa will travel to Beijing on May 29 to raise this figure to US$ 9 billion. Brazil's aid, the fruit of Alberto Fernandez's lightning visit to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has so far been limited to a pat on the shoulder.

Food importsIn the list of measures against inflation there are also heterodox measures. To encourage consumption and lower the amount of pesos in cash, the Government will subsidize credit for the purchase of durable goods in installments. Against the rise in food prices, imports will be opened, an unprecedented decision in one of the world's largest producers. The Central Fruit and Vegetable Market will be in charge of foreign purchases, which will operate through a trust. In addition, a Trade Operations Analysis Unit will be created to "monitor the purchase and sale of goods and services".

The Government's bet is to avoid an economic outburst that would dilapidate any possibility of electoral triumph in October. The crisis has ended up cracking Peronism, in a long process of political flagellation started at the beginning of the administration, in 2019. The president, Alberto Fernández, has not spoken to his vice-president, Cristina Kirchner, for months. Both finally surrendered to Minister Massa, who never hid his presidential aspirations.

The disbandment reached the provinces where Peronism governs, which have separated their local elections from the national ones so as not to be infected by the general disaster. Last week elections were held in Neuquén and Río Negro, in Patagonia, and candidates more or less aligned with the Casa Rosada won. This Sunday, Salta, Tierra del Fuego and La Pampa will vote, where the Government expects good results. A Court ruling suspended the elections in San Juan and Tucumán, strongholds of Peronism where the local caudillos were seeking reelections at odds with the Constitution.

title: Argentina announces economic measures to counter rising prices
text:
Argentina will adjust interest rates to curb the dollarization of its economy, the Central Bank will have more freedom to control foreign currency and agreements with the IMF will be accelerated.

Those are some of the measures advanced on Sunday by the country's Economy Ministry, which will announce more initiatives during the week, after one of the worst inflation figures was released on Friday.

Argentina's Central Bank will adjust the rate, increase "intervention in the foreign exchange market and will manage the pace of the crawl" the progressive devaluation of the Argentine peso, the Economy Ministry said on Sunday.

This places Argentina in second place in the World Bank's ranking of countries with the highest food inflation after Lebanon.

Economy Minister Sergio Massa's team spent the whole of Saturday in meetings and advanced a package of economic measures to control price increases.

Economic analysts pointed out that April's consumer price index is the highest monthly inflation rate since April 2002, when the rise in prices exceeded 10%.

The Ministry announced the acceleration of the agreements with the IMF, the China swaps (Massa will travel to Beijing on May 29) and the guarantee scheme of the so-called BRICS block (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) for imports and currency exchange with Brazil.

There will be incentives to sustain the level of domestic consumption by promoting the consumption of products of national origin, such as decreases in interest rates for credit cards or the increase of reimbursements to vulnerable sectors for consumption with debit cards.

There will also be measures to sustain the country's level of economic activity, such as tax relief for small and medium-sized companies, elimination of tariffs and the creation of dumping and protection rules to improve competitiveness and reduce import prices of certain products.

Approvals for the importation of capital goods will be accelerated and a new Trade Operations Analysis Unit will be created to coordinate with other national agencies and be able to respond more quickly to price increases and changes and speed up foreign trade, among other measures.

In addition, the Central Market will adopt a new role as a direct food importer with the objective of reducing the effective retail price of fresh produce such as fruits, vegetables and meats as well as non-perishable dry goods.

Soaring prices increased poverty, which now affects almost 40% of the population, or some 18.5 million people. Child poverty rose to 54.2%, covering six million children under the age of 15.

Inflation is one of the main concerns of Argentines, together with insecurity, according to public opinion polls published in the run-up to the October presidential elections, in which current President Alberto Fernández will not run.

The long drought that the country is experiencing damaged crops by reducing the inflow of foreign currency, which is coupled with the strong depreciation of the peso in the financial markets in a context of strict capital controls.

By Jorge Otaola and Maximilian Heath

BUENOS AIRES, May 14 (Reuters) - Argentina's government announced a package of measures to rein in soaring inflation and support the wobbly peso currency on Sunday, including rate adjustments, more interventions in the exchange market and expedited deals with creditors.

The measures include an interest rate hike by the central bank, the economy ministry said in a statement. The ministry did not elaborate, but an official source told Reuters the hike would be 600 basis points, bringing the rate up to 97%.

The rate hike will take effect Monday, the source added.

The South American nation is battling to bring down inflation that hit 109% on an annual basis in April. It also faces tumbling confidence in the peso and dwindling foreign currency reserves that are threatening the government's finances.

The central bank will also increase its intervention in the foreign-exchange market and double down on its currency devaluation plan, the ministry said.

An agreement with the International Monetary Fund to dole out funds to the cash-strapped nation will be sped up as well, the ministry added.

More measures are set to be announced in coming days, according to the ministry.

President Alberto Fernandez's government is looking to bring the economic situation under control as elections near, with opinion polls showing flagging support for the ruling Peronist party. title: Argentina announces an increase in interest rate and  foreign exchange  market  intervention  to tackle inflation
text:

In addition, it will seek to accelerate the agreements with the International Monetary Fund, the exchange of currencies with China and the conversations with the BRICS block.

title: Argentina  announces 97% interest rate package and more  foreign exchange intervention
text:
The Argentine government will announce on Monday (15) a package of measures to try to contain inflation and stabilize the peso against the dollar.

According to Reuters news agency and the Argentinean newspapers Clarín and La Nacíon, the basic interest rate will rise from 91% to 97% per year. If confirmed, this will be the second rate increase in less than a month. On April 27th the rate rose from 81 percent to 91 percent, the highest level in 20 years.

At the same time, Argentina's Central Bank is expected to increase its intervention in the exchange market in order to stabilize the peso. According to Argentinian publications, the measure is aimed at meeting the request of the IMF (International Monetary Fund) and accelerating agreements with the IMF, China and Brazil.

The package was defined after meetings between Economy Minister Sergio Massa and Central Bank President Miguel Pesce.

Currently, Argentina's inflation is at 109% in the accumulated between May last year and April this year. Last month alone, inflation was 8.4%, twice as high as in the whole of last year in Brazil (4.2%).

According to the newspapers Clarín and La Nacíon, the government is still expected to announce other measures on Monday morning (15th). One of them is to negotiate with the bank of the Brics to facilitate currency exchange with Brazil.

Massa is expected to travel to Beijing on May 29 to try to bring more resources to the country. Internally, the Argentinian government is expected to lower interest rates in the "Agora 12" program, with the aim of stimulating the consumption of national products.

According to the newspaper La Nacíon, there will also be an increase in cashback on debit cards for payments made by the most vulnerable population. The publication states that other measures may be released this week to complement the package.

Last week, Massa had already announced increases in pensions and social benefits after 90 days, as well as in the floor for income tax payments.

If a year ago those earning more than 225,000 Argentine pesos had to file a tax return, now only those earning more than 506,000 (the equivalent of about US$1,100 at the parallel exchange rate) will have to do so. The increase is 125%, which is above the accumulated inflation rate.

Social Security and the scholarships given by the government to low-income families also had an increase of 130%, above inflation in the last year - a real increase of 7%, according to Massa. As a result, an Argentinian pensioner will earn from 121,407 pesos (US$260) in June.

title: New obstacles for importers: the government "steps on every dollar" and stretches deadlines to the limit
text:
The Central Bank of Argentinaintervened again in the foreign exchange regulations to modify the terms from which companies that were exempted from the procedures that until now affected most of the imports become part of the general regime.

Until now, there was a universe of products -health industry, pharmaceuticals, those affected by the fight against Covid 19 and even capital goods- that submitted an affidavit informing of their exemption.

But the limitations and eventual extensions in the terms for payment abroad are not limited only to those basic inputs of Covid, medical products and medicines or inputs of the pharmaceutical industry.

This is established in the new communication A 7766 of the Central Bank, dated Thursday, May 11, which explains in its point 1 that "in order to give access to the foreign exchange market within the framework of the provisions of points 8.1. to 8.6. of Communication 'A' 7622 and complementary communications, in order to make payments with pending customs entry record for transactions supported by SIRA declarations officialized as from May 12, the entities must additionally verify that the corresponding SIRA declaration in 'OUTGOING' status has been assigned a term of 0 (zero) calendar days".

An exploration of the details of the exceptions referred to (points 8.1 to 8.6 of communication "A" 7622) shows that in addition to the health industry, petroleum products and inputs for the production of fuels are also affected.

In the paroxysm of the regulation, the impact even reaches construction materials used in public works, such as the necessary and promoted Néstor Kirchner Gas Pipeline. Zero days to access the market and cancel the goods.

While before the regulation, the presentation of a sworn statement justifying the exception enabled them to automatically enter the foreign exchange market -even when the regulation established that the product had to wait between 60 and 90 days- now the SIRA must specifically state "0 (zero) days".

"Now those SIRAs have to say 0 (zero) days to be able to close exchange. This generated that not a single payment of this type of goods has been made", an operator of the foreign exchange market explained to iProfesional.

"What until yesterday were exceptions, today they are paid on the date set by the Secretariat of Commerce, like any other cargo", confirmed the Chamber of Importers.

If the answer given by the agency is "0 (zero) days", it means that the company can access the market and cancel the goods whenever it wants, even before customs clearance (nationalization or entry of the product). On the other hand, if they say 30, 60, 90 or 120 days, it is necessary to wait that term -from the customs clearance- for the transfer.

That is to say, from the moment an order is placed abroad, and that company starts to manufacture it (with the time it takes, but in the case of capital goods it may take several months), dispatches it, ships it and arrives in Argentina, it may take another 60 to 90 days to be able to remit payment, according to a "trickle-down" criterion of the Secretariat of Commerce.

In a new confession of the discretionality that will mark the payment terms for products that were "exempted", the Government is stepping on every dollar it can, stretching the terms to the maximum.

title: U.S. would support IMF to speed up loan delivery to Argentina
text:
May 12 (Bloomberg) -- The administration of U.S. President Joseph R. Biden would support accelerating disbursements under the International Monetary Fund's $44 billion program for Argentina if the nation's authorities can successfully negotiate a new schedule with the international lender, according to U.S. officials familiar with the matter.

Under the current program, Argentina will receive $10.6 billion from the IMF between June and December. However, the South American nation, pressured by dwindling international reserves, out-of-control inflation and a record agricultural drought, is seeking to advance some or all of that IMF financing to June.

The United States would support frontloading the resources because it sees the need to prevent Argentina's economic crisis from worsening, said the officials, who asked not to be identified without permission to speak publicly on the matter.

The Argentine government plans to argue to the IMF that the severe drought the nation is suffering is beyond its control, and it needs the funds as soon as possible to control the crisis.

U.S. support is important, given its status as the IMF's largest shareholder and the fund's desire to make decisions by consensus.

But negotiating an early distribution of the loan with IMF staff will not be an easy task for Argentina. The fund is likely to ask for conditions that could be difficult for the country to meet, and Argentina has a long history of failing to meet targets set by the IMF.

Another U.S. official cautioned that the United States would have to review any staffing arrangement and consult with IMF leaders and other board members before taking an official position.

The U.S. Treasury Department, the National Security Council and Argentina's Economy Ministry declined to comment.

Argentina's bond prices have fallen sharply three years after the South American nation restructured $65 billion of its foreign debt.

An IMF spokeswoman said the fund continues to work very closely with the Argentine authorities to strengthen the country's program in the context of the drought, and that discussions on the next review are ongoing and continuing in a constructive manner.

Argentina is the IMF's largest borrower and has a complicated history with the fund after 22 different programs over nearly 70 years did little to fix a crisis-prone economy.

The current program is already off track with the government likely to miss key targets through the end of March, while annual inflation hit 104% and the peso plunged on parallel markets. Those setbacks forced the authorities to go back to the drawing board to review the loan.

Argentina also faces a volatile presidential election this year and accepting a looser financial program could be seen by the opposition as a favor to the government ahead of the October vote.

Complicated history

Although unusual by its standards, the IMF has advanced cash to Argentina before. In 2018, the IMF approved advancing disbursements to the government of former President Mauricio Macri as the economy plummeted into a currency crisis triggered by another significant drought. However, more cash upfront did not stabilize the economy and the program was suspended around the 2019 presidential election.

To complicate matters further, Argentina's Vice President Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner, who over the years has repeatedly criticized the IMF, last week blamed the existing program for the country's economic malaise, complaining that the fund's rules prevented the central bank from intervening to stem the peso's slide.

Argentina's economy is facing one of its most severe moments with drought sending activity into recession and international reserves falling even after the Fund disbursed $5.4 billion in new funds in early April, bringing disbursements under the Fund's expanded facility to $28.9 billion.

--with assistance from Patrick Gillespie and Scott Squires.

title: Fixed term in dollars yields 5% in the U.S. but only a fraction in Argentina: why
text:
Rate hikes in the United States caused one-month placements to yield an effective rate of 5% or more per annum. In Argentina, yields are close to 0% for savings and time deposits. Entities even avoid accepting placements in the U.S. currency due to the complexities of re-lending those funds.

Despite the BCRA rate hike, corporate loans grew for the first time in 9 months.

Santi Maratea already exceeded $ 720 million with its collection in Mercado Pago but still does not generate interest: why?

The local market adds an additional difficulty: today there is a continuous dripping of dollar placements in banks, with a fall in deposits that reaches u$s 1,200 million in five weeks.

What is happening? There is a high correlation between the level of Central Bank reserves and the stock of deposits in banks. Savers, seeing that the monetary entity is in difficulties as far as foreign currency is concerned, are infected by the prevailing uncertainty and some choose to withdraw their holdings.

The IMF spoke: the signal to make the program more flexible and a visit that Argentina avoids

The BCRA's interventions in the market to maintain the official exchange rate without abrupt jumps made its coffers weaken and there are even "negative net reserves", which adds more doubts to savers.

Remember that banks are obliged to deposit a percentage of the deposits they receive from savers in the BCRA as liquidity requirements.

The BCRA can obtain yields of 4% per annum against US Treasury bonds with those dollars transferred by the banks. For the entity presided by Miguel Pesce, it is pure profit on the u$s 11,386 million it has in its portfolio due to the non-interest-bearing reserve requirements on dollar placements in banks.

The departure of the then Minister Martín Guzmán from the Treasury Palace and his replacement by the ephemeral Silvina Batakis also generated a fall in deposits that stopped at u$s 14,000 million.

Today the stock is around u$s 15 billion. The arrival of Sergio Massa and the launching of the soybean dollar I and II allowed the recovery of deposits to well over u$s 16 billion.

Another factor that triggered investors' distrust was the launching of the debt swap for government agencies with the "pesification" of their holdings, an accursed word in the local market. This launch coincided with the beginning of the first withdrawals of dollars from the entities.

In the previous occasions when there was an outflow of funds, the process stabilized at some point. The system is very liquid.

In any case, it is still an issue that is closely followed, especially when in the meantime there are presidential elections that add uncertainty. In fact, the transfer of pesos to dollars is a classic action in the run-up to every election in Argentina.

Massa: "We need political order for there to be economic order".

A factor that is repeated year after year is the increase of deposits in December, but for tax reasons. The rates to be paid for Personal Property are lower due to the holding of dollars in bank accounts than in foreign accounts.

In the short term, it is practically impossible for yields on dollar deposits in Argentina to come close to U.S. yields. Then the demand for dollar loans (limited to exporters) will rise and cause rates to rise. Depositors in banks are looking for custody rather than yields. Although today doubts are gnawing at them.

title: Massa called on businessmen and trade unionists to reach agreements for economic and social progress
text:
The Minister of Economy, Sergio Massa, today called on businessmen and trade unionists to reach agreements to "define a process of economic and social development" in Argentina, and highlighted that with energy, mining and the agro-industrial sector the country will not have foreign currency problems in the coming years. Massa made this appeal during a meeting organized by the Ibero-American Institute for Education and Productivity (OEI), which took place this noon, informed the Treasury Palace. Among those present were Luis Scasso, director of OEI Argentina; José Urtubey, director of Celulosa Argentina; Héctor Daer, CGT General Secretary; Gerardo Martínez, General Secretary of Uocra and member of the Board of Directors for the ILO Workers' Group; Rodrigo Pérez Graziano, president of PSA GROUPE-Peugeot-Citroen Argentina; and Gustavo Idigoras, head of the Chamber of the Oil Industry and Grain Exporters' Center (Ciara/CEC), among others.

 For Massa "if we do not understand that beyond the fight of political, economic, social, business and trade union leaders at the time of public debate, in some issues we have to choose a development path for the next 10 or 20 years, we will fall from the possibility of being global players". The minister made a reflection by assuring that "uncertainty may generate anger against the political class, which in turn may represent a candidate" that channels that discontent. In view of this, "my question is: is it not also time for all political actors to ask ourselves what we did wrong for someone with these characteristics to emerge? And when I say actors, I don't mean political party leaders, I mean businessmen actors, I mean social actors", Massa asked. He said that those leaders "are not aliens" who come to Argentina "and sit in the political parties", but that "they emerge from each of our communities, cities, provinces, states and in any case if we do not have the leadership we want it is because those who believe they have more capacity to occupy that place, do not occupy it and others with less capabilities end up doing it". "That inexorably forces us to think that in order to change things we have to participate", Massa stressed. He stressed that from the economic leadership "we feel that our responsibility is to intervene to guarantee stability and we understand that, in a country like Argentina, sometimes, from the Central Bank, from the Ministry of Economy and from the different instruments that the State has to guarantee economic stability, we must intervene". "If Argentina has high production levels in these sectors, the process of accumulation of reserves, even with the levels of indebtedness that the country has, is clearly guaranteed for the next few years", said the head of the Treasury Palace. (Télam)

title: Schiaretti on the campaign trail: "If we do not put together a coalition that overcomes the rift, Milei is likely to grow".
text:
Already launched as a pre-candidate for president to compete in the next Paso 2023 elections in Argentina, the governor of Córdoba, Juan Schiaretti began a tour of the local media where he ratifies the main guidelines on which his campaign will be based from this province.

After reiterating that he will be a candidate "against the rift", he said that the coalition he intends to lead together with other national leaders and political referents of the country "has nothing to do with Kirchnerism".

"Kirchnerism always wanted to colonize Córdoba but it could not do it, and it will not do it either", he assured in a dialogue with Cadena 3. "Argentina has always been centralist, there is a view of the country from Amba. Our space will try to express the position of those who work, those who produce, the productive interior", he added.

And then he listed the axes on which Argentina should work: "The first thing is to recover the institutional functioning of Argentina, stop persecuting and denigrating those who do not think like you do, as in the case of the Supreme Court or the media".

"Then we have to dedicate ourselves to a serious economic stabilization, not patches on patches that are a resounding failure, Kirchernism has been failing since this government started", said Schiaretti.

And then he showed his concern for the inflationary indexes: "I vote so that we do not have an inflationary flash, because of the impact on the people, I hope we do not have one that deteriorates people's lives even more. But I also do not see any actions taken by the national government to lower inflation".

"We have to seriously attack the fiscal deficit in Argentina, from all angles, without this meaning a wild adjustment", he added.

Schiaretti on his government's self-criticismWhen asked about the self-criticism he can make regarding his administration, the governor mentioned, "We have had mistakes, of course, but every time we recognize it, we act accordingly, we try to solve them".

"To point out mistakes there is the opposition, we as a government are obliged to solve them," he said.

"I was never arbitrary and if I ever was I apologize to the person who may consider it so. I have made mistakes, surely but they have never been in bad faith. I will be a circumstance in the political life in Córdoba", said Schiarreti.

And he added: "I never believed it, I did not flaunt it, I am the same boy from Talleres Oeste who walked around that neighborhood when I was a kid," he said.

"I regret having smoked", he finished.

Schiaretti on the fight against drugsThe governor and pre-candidate also pronounced himself in favor of the intervention of federal forces to fight the drug advance in Argentina. "There must be border control, more participation of federal forces in the fight and control over the funds managed by those involved in drug organizations," he added.

And he said that another way is to intervene in the neighborhood organizations to prevent the drug traffickers "from taking over those sectors".

Schiaretti on the public employees' bargaining agreementsThe governor also referred to the delays that were generated in the negotiations with public employees, both with teachers and with the health sector: "This is absolutely logical, because we have a galloping inflation and that is what has caused us to take so long to reach an agreement. In the current situation we have with prices, it is very difficult to make long-term plans".

Schiaretti expressed his opinion on the impact of Javier Milei's candidacyThe pre-candidate for President for the next Paso elections expressed his opinion on Javier Milei's candidacy: "It is the expression of the rejection to the political class. If those of us who think about work are not capable of putting together a political coalition leaving aside those who are inside the rift, both in Kirchnerism and in Juntos por el Cambio, it is likely that Milei's figure will continue to grow".

And about this candidate's proposal to dollarize the economy, he added: "Dollarization is a miraculous measure without any kind of support. The country needs a stable currency, independence of the Central Bank and fiscal measures".

Schiaretti on Martín LlaryoraRegarding the gubernatorial candidate who aspires to succeed him in office for the coalition Hacemos Unidos por Córdoba, Martín Llaryora, Schiaretti showed his support and explained the reasons: "I think he is the person who has shown youth and experience in management quality. He gives certainty and seriousness, he is capable of maintaining all the good things and improving what needs to be done".

Our audited consolidated financial statements as of December 31, 2022 and 2021 and for each of the years ended December 31, 2022, 2021 and 2020, comprehensively recognize the effects of variations in the purchasing power of currency through the application of the method to restate financial statements in constant currency established by the International Accounting Standard 29, or IAS 29, as Argentina is considered a hyperinflationary economy starting July 1, 2018.

Financial information presented in constant currency

IAS 29, Financial Reporting in Hyperinflationary Economies ("IAS 29") requires that the financial statements of an entity whose functional currency is one of a hyperinflationary economy be measured in terms of the current unit of measurement at the closing date of the financial statements, regardless of whether they are based on the historical cost method or the current cost method. This requirement also includes the comparative information of the financial statements.

In order to conclude that an economy is "hyperinflationary," IAS 29 outlines a series of factors, including the existence of an accumulated inflation rate in three years that is approximately or exceeds 100%. As of December 31, 2018, Argentina reported a cumulative three-year inflation rate greater than 100% and therefore financial information published as from that date should be adjusted for inflation in accordance with IAS 29. The inflation of the subsequent fiscal years continues to be high and above the 100% accumulated inflation trend for three consecutive years. Therefore, our audited consolidated financial statements and the financial information included in this annual report have been stated in terms of the measuring unit current at the end of the reporting year.

In accordance with IAS 29, the amounts in the financial statements that have not been stated in constant currency as of the end of the reporting period must be restated by application of a general price index. To that end and in the manner established in FACPCE's Resolution JG No. 539/18, coefficients have been applied that are calculated on the basis of indices published by the FACPCE, resulting from combining national the consumer prices index ( Índice de Precios al Consumidor-IPC ), or CPI, published by the Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas y Censos (the National Statistics and Census Institute), or INDEC, starting on January 1, 2017 and, looking back, domestic wholesale prices index ( Índice de Precios Internos al por Mayor-IPIM ), or WPI, published by the INDEC or, if none is available, consumer price indices published by the General Directorate of Statistics and Censuses in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. The variation in the index applied to restate our audited consolidated financial statements for the years ended as of December 31, 2022, 2021 and 2020 was 94.8%, 50.9% and 36.1%, respectively.

• aggravation of a financial crisis in several countries in the region;

As a way to alleviate the ensuing crisis, in June 2018, Argentina and the IMF agreed to a stand-by loan for US$50.0 billion with duration of 36 months with the IMF (the "Stand-By Agreement") to back up the economic program, and which was extended to US$57.1 billion in September 2018. The IMF requested the Argentine government to implement the following measures: (i) reduce the primary deficit to 1.3% in 2019 and achieve the primary fiscal balance by 2020; and (ii) strengthen the autonomy of the BCRA. The reduction of the deficit implied a cut in public spending, reduction of energy and transportation subsidies, reduction of public works, transfers to the provinces, among other measures.

The Extended Fund Facility Arrangement seeks to continue creating the necessary stability conditions to address existing structural challenges and to strengthen the foundations for sustainable and inclusive growth. In accordance to the Extended Fund Facility Arrangement, Argentina will be paying its debt from 2026 to 2034. If current levels of fiscal deficits are not reduced, the Argentine economy could be adversely affected, negatively impacting our business and results of operation.

In the past, Argentina has had important macroeconomic imbalances, including frequent and critical fiscal deficits. The Argentine government has had yearly fiscal deficit during approximately 90% of the period comprising 1961 to 2022 (48 years out of 53), which has led to very vulnerable macroeconomic conditions. The Argentine government has financed its fiscal deficit mainly in two ways: (i) by issuing foreign debt, which has historically led to rapid increments in national debt levels; and (ii) by monetary emission through the BCRA, which has led to periods of high inflation and, even in some cases, hyperinflation. Historically, inflation has materially undermined the Argentine economy and the Argentine government's ability to create conditions for long-term economic growth. In recent years, Argentina has experienced high inflation rates.

Since 2008, the Argentine economy has been subject to strong inflationary pressures that, according to private sector analysts, reached an average annual rate of 28.2% between 2010 and 2015. In December 2015, the new administration suspended the publication of indexes and statistics and, after implementing certain methodological reforms and adjusting certain macroeconomic statistics, resumed its publication of the CPI in June 2016. Based on the new and revised information provided by INDEC, inflation reached an annual rate of 36.1% in 2020, 50,9% in 2021 and 94.8% in 2022.

The Argentine government has implemented programs to control inflation and monitor prices for essential goods and services, including attempts to freeze the price of certain supermarket products by means of price support arrangements between the government and the private sector. These programs, however, do not address the structural causes for Argentina's inflation and, consequently, failed to reduce inflation.

The government reported a primary fiscal deficit of 1.7% GDP in 2019, 6.5% GDP in 2020, 3% in 2021 and 2.4% in 2022. However, one of the principal aims of the Staff-Level Agreement is a gradual reduction of the fiscal deficit. It includes a strategy with the objective of reaching a primary fiscal deficit of 2,5% of GDP in 2022, and expect it to be reduced to 1.9% of GDP in 2023 and 0.9 of GDP in 2024.
